hints: Look at what functional groups are present in the starting molecule and what type of linkage appears in L.
Notice that 5-hydroxypentanoic acid has both an -OH and a -COOH in the same molecule, so it can react with itself to form an ester link.
Recall what small molecule is always lost when an ester forms, and what catalyst is normally used for esterification.
walkthrough:
**Identify the starting material**

Think of 5-hydroxypentanoic acid as HO-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2-COOH. It has an alcohol group at one end and a carboxylic acid group at the other end.

Structure idea:
$$\text{HO-(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{-COOH}$$

**Recognise intramolecular esterification**

The -OH can attack the -COOH in the same molecule to close a 6-membered ring. This forms a cyclic ester, called a lactone, which is compound L.

General esterification:
$$\text{R-COOH + HO-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-COO-R' + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check each statement**

Statement 2 is correct because ester formation eliminates water. Statement 3 is correct because esterification is acid catalysed, typically by concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Statement 1 is incorrect because acidified dichromate(VI) is an oxidising agent, and no oxidation or reduction happens here. It is a condensation reaction, not a redox reaction.

**Conclude the combination**

Only statements 2 and 3 are correct. That combination matches the option for 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are true, but statement 1 is false because no oxidant is needed for lactone formation.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 is wrong because acidified sodium dichromate(VI) oxidises primary alcohols and aldehydes, but here the alcohol simply forms an ester with no change in oxidation state.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is true because intramolecular esterification is a condensation with loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement 3 is true because concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is the standard acid catalyst for esterification.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only statement 1 is correct. In fact statement 1 is the only false statement. Students choosing this may confuse lactone formation with oxidation of the alcohol to a carboxylic acid.
